requirements.requirement: The installer works when invoked by POSIX /bin/sh, including with a destination path containing spaces.
requirements.summary: The revised installer passed /bin/sh syntax validation and successfully installed into “destination with spaces” when invoked explicitly through /bin/sh. Functionality remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Both supplied templates are installed with contents intact, and the installed launcher is executable.
requirements.summary: Direct comparisons and matching SHA-256 hashes establish byte-for-byte template and launcher preservation. The installed launcher had mode 755 and executed successfully, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: The installer reports failure when the destination cannot be populated.
requirements.summary: Using a regular file as the destination produced status 1, emitted an explanatory error, retained the blocker, and did not falsely populate the destination.
Two successive installations completed successfully, restored deliberately altered content and permissions, preserved all expected file contents, and left the expected three installed files.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were observed before and after the work and restart. The solution uses existing POSIX shell utilities, with no package or platform upgrade recorded.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it captures a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, observed unavailability during reboot, a different post-restart boot ID, recovered SSH, and persisted functional data. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition. The only notable issue is minor retained test residue under /tmp.

operational_hygiene.summary: The task-relevant installer edit, temporary backup, functional tests, deliberate idempotency perturbations, and mandatory restart all had clear purposes. The backup was removed, and the deliberately altered installed content and mode were fully restored. However, the executor did not clean the bounded test tree created by cmd-a50c86c423f44986, subsequently modified by cmd-d1e1f42f01574c43 and cmd-b850fac37bc14836, and reused by cmd-d968cb17199f432f. The after-executor snapshot confirms that /tmp/branch-report-posix-test and its spaced-path subdirectory remained; the blocker file created by the failure test also was not shown as removed. This is low-risk executor-caused test residue. No damaged package state, unsafe exposure, or conflicting service state is evident.
